uncited: Unlike standard volume rendering which takes density directly, this approach derives density from the distance to the implicit surface, enabling the representation of open surfaces and varying thickness through an exponential falloff [1282-sdf-to-density-conversion.md].

This conversion typically involves mapping the signed distance $d$ to an intermediate density $\rho$ using a piecewise exponential function controlled by parameters $\alpha$ (scaling) and $\beta$ (falloff/sharpness) [1282-sdf-to-density-conversion.md].
The final density $\sigma$ is derived from $\rho$ and the ray segment length $\Delta t$ to ensure resolution independence [1282-sdf-to-density-conversion.md].

This process requires an initial distance transform followed by smoothing to ensure the result is a valid SDF (satisfying the Eikonal equation $|\nabla d| = 1$) while preserving the topological sign of the level set [1583-constrained-jacobi-smoothing-for-sdfs.md].
- **Definition**: An end-to-end method to optimize both SDF and reconstructed meshes jointly, predicting surface meshes from images.
